title: wirevocab's live herdr drift guard can be served stale from a warm cache
description:
The drift test diffs the pinned herd vocabulary against the installed herdr binary — a host input outside the module, reached through a subprocess. cmd/go never rechecks outside-module inputs (computeTestInputsID skips them at hashing time, deliberately), so on any host with a warm go test cache a herdr upgrade cannot invalidate this package's cached pass. That matters because CI never runs the guard at all (no herdr on a public-repo runner): the operator's and worker hosts — exactly the machines with warm caches — are the only places the pin's freshness is ever proven, and the test's own comment claimed every suite executes it. No read the test could perform closes it: outside-module reads are never rechecked, in-process or not. The structural fix is keeping the package uncached in the gate (a [testing.commands] + Makefile gate-recipe change, which must stay byte-identical under TestTheGateTargetMatchesTheDeclaredGate), or accepting the residual now documented in drift_test.go's comment. Demonstrated by TestACachedPassCanHideAnEditToAFileOutsideTheModule and the scratch experiment behind it.
evidence: internal/herd/wirevocab/drift_test.go:65; cmd/go/internal/test/test.go computeTestInputsID ("Do not recheck files outside the module, GOPATH, or GOROOT root")
